## Start here

Two afternoons of four hours, including breaks. No R or statistics experience is assumed.
You will start with small interactive exercises, then build your own reproducible notebook.

BDNF is a protein involved in neuronal plasticity. Researchers measured proteins in the nuclear fraction of mouse cortex after a learning protocol. Our first comparison uses control-genotype mice given saline or memantine. A change in one assay signal does not establish improved memory.

**First question:** Does memantine change the BDNF assay signal in control mice exposed to the same learning protocol?

1. Download [the student project](statistics_lab_student.zip), unzip it, and open `Statistics_lab.Rproj` in RStudio.
2. Follow [setup](notebooks/00_setup.html). In the Console, run `source("scripts/run_pilot.R")`.
3. Complete the interactive learnr tutorial in the browser. Submit your code and download your notebook regularly.
4. Continue in RStudio with [statistical analysis](notebooks/03_statistical_analysis.html), opening its matching `.Rmd` file to work.
5. On day 2, open [your investigation](notebooks/04_investigation.html) and its `.Rmd` template. Submit your completed integrated HTML notebook.

The HTML pages above are reading previews. **The interactive learnr tutorial requires a running
R session**; opening an HTML file or a GitHub page does not start its exercise engine.

## Preview and data

- [Tutorial reading preview](tutorial_preview.html): explanations, worked starters and sample plots; launch R for controls and editable exercises.
- [Data dictionary](data/dictionary.html): what a row means, units and preparation rules.
- [Study CSV](data/study.csv): first-day animal table.
- [Investigation CSV](data/investigation.csv): second-day table.
- [Original dataset](https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/342/mice+protein+expression).

Keep your work in `notebooks/`. The Source editor holds your saved recipe; the Console executes
commands; Knit makes the HTML you submit. Ask for help early. Explaining a result is more
important than remembering a command.

Day 1 builds towards **More rows, more evidence?**: identify animals behind the measurements, reveal their dots, and investigate why copying data cannot create biological replication.
